artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained Psiaki’s complaint and held that the CPC Session erred by ordaining and installing officers elected at a February 5, 2023 congregational meeting where the congregation’s bylaw excluded communing members under 18 from voting. Reading BCO 6-4, 25-1, and 25-7 together, the SJC ruled that all communing members are entitled to vote and that local bylaws cannot impose an age restriction; the “good and regular standing” language addresses censure, not age. The decision did not annul the completed ordination/installation, but required future elections and installations to comply with the Constitution.

artifacts.synopsis: Smith complained that Northeast Presbytery failed to provide pastoral care after dissolving Grace Presbyterian Church. The SJC rejected Presbytery's objections that the complaint lacked supporting reasons or was barred by Smith's protest, held it in order, but denied it on the merits. Distinguishing the pastoral 'power of order' from judicial 'power of jurisdiction,' the SJC ruled that the Constitution neither requires nor permits a presbytery to retain jurisdiction over individual members of a dissolved particular church, and that pastoral care of former members is generally discretionary; on these facts, Presbytery's efforts satisfied any duty.

artifacts.synopsis: A member challenged Presbytery’s refusal, after investigation, to try four elders on favoritism charges and its ruling that her related complaint was out of order because dissolution of her church ended her PCA membership. The SJC denied the first item because BCO 31-2 permits declining process when investigation raises no strong presumption of guilt. It sustained the second: jurisdiction properly invoked while a communicant member is not lost through a later status change. No remand was expressly ordered.

artifacts.synopsis: Smith challenged Northeast Presbytery’s ruling that his complaint was untimely and unconstitutional after it dissolved Grace Church and indefinitely postponed a proposed Braintree mission. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded it for Presbytery adjudication. The May action first revealed Presbytery’s view that former members were outside the PCA, so the June complaint was timely. BCO 11-4 neither barred nor itself required care; responsibility arose here from the April referral to Presbytery’s missions committee. Care need not take the form of a mission, and mere dissolution alone would not create that responsibility.

artifacts.title: Membership status and session authority upon dissolution of a congregation

matches.evidence: Upon dissolution of a congregation, the session terminates, membership in the visible church is dissolved for those not transferred, and Presbytery may not unilaterally assign members to other churches.

artifacts.title: Mandatory prior notice requirement for congregational withdrawal from PCA

matches.evidence: A proposed notice requirement for withdrawal conflicted with BCO 25-11, which allows a church to withdraw at any time for reasons it deems sufficient.
